group.passage:
Nearly everyone finds that prices displayed in odd fractions, like $9.99, are meant to encourage the belief that an item costs significantly less than the whole number, although it is just a penny less. Most people claim not to be fooled by this tactic. They say they simply round up the figure to $10. [[1]] Studies have shown that not only does the penny difference increases sales disproportionately, but many more pricing strategies are also effective despite working against consumers’ best interests. Together, these are known as psychological pricing.
Psychological pricing is a strategy that uses pricing to influence a customer’s spending or shopping habits to make more or higher-value sales. [[2]] Maybe that’s saving money, investing in the highest quality item, or getting a good deal. Psychological pricing plays on the fact that consumers rarely know what something should cost. Most often the way they are able to determine if something is a good deal is by getting it for a lower price than normally listed or by comparing it to similar products in the same category. [[3]] They pay less attention to the fractional, right-hand part of a price than on the more significant, larger digits.
Indeed, social psychologists have found that people do not always make decisions in their best interest on the basis of reason. They might hold diverse ideas simultaneously and adopt various forms of rationalization and self-justification to ease the resulting tension. [[4]] They are conscious of the importance of saving for retirement, but they still prefer to enjoy a more luxurious lifestyle at the moment. The fact that psychological pricing works, even though almost everyone sees through the trick, demonstrates the significant role that subconscious desires and thoughts play in economic decisions.

options_bank.A: Also, psychological pricing may work because consumers try to save time and effort in their calculations.
options_bank.B: The fact is, this strategy would not be used continuously for so many years if it were not effective.
options_bank.C: For example, it makes sense to save money for retirement, yet many people fail to do it.
options_bank.D: The goal is to meet a customer’s psychological need or expectation for something.
